outputs: Generated facts, entities, and answers for coreference questions.
The paper evaluates performance on classification outputs such as sentiment, stance, causal relations, and bias avoidance, which are not traditional NLG tasks involving free-form text generation.

changes_made.explanation: Changed answer from Yes to No because this paper focuses on classification tasks and reasoning rather than natural language generation. All metadata was removed since none of it relates to NLG tasks.

Normalized metrics to base forms (ROUGE-L → ROUGE, relaxed F1-score → F1) and added F1 which was implicitly mentioned as 'relaxed F1-score'. The paper uses these metrics to evaluate classification performance.
No LLMs are used as judges/evaluators in this paper. ChatGPT/GPT models are only used as the model being evaluated (generation model), not as evaluators.
No human evaluation is conducted in this paper. The paper only uses automatic evaluation metrics.

overall_notes: This paper focuses on experience transfer for classification and reasoning tasks using LLMs, not natural language generation. The primary contribution is a framework for transferring task-solving experiences between different classification tasks. All evaluation is automatic using classification metrics (Accuracy, ROUGE, F1) on classification outputs.
